channel.title: Kafka | System Design
channel.description: In-depth system design tutorials — from zero to millions of users. Written for engineers who want to understand how large-scale systems actually work.

item.title: Design an Ad Click Event Aggregation System
item.author: abhaypratap3537@gmail.com (Abhay)
item.description: A billion clicks a day, and the numbers become invoices. Event time versus processing time, watermarks, exactly-once as an actual requirement rather than a nice-to-have — with an interactive watermark simulator for the accuracy-versus-latency trade at the heart of every streaming system.

item.title: Design a Metrics Monitoring and Alerting System
item.author: abhaypratap3537@gmail.com (Abhay)
item.description: Ten million metrics, one year of retention, and a write load that never stops. Why a general-purpose database is the wrong answer, how Gorilla gets 16 bytes down to 1.37, and the cardinality bomb that kills more monitoring systems than any other cause — with an interactive calculator.
item.content:encoded:
Ten million metrics, one year of retention, and a write load that never stops. Why a general-purpose database is the wrong answer, how Gorilla gets 16 bytes down to 1.37, and the cardinality bomb that kills more monitoring systems than any other cause — with an interactive calculator.

item.title: Design a Distributed Message Queue
item.author: abhaypratap3537@gmail.com (Abhay)
item.description: Why a plain append-only file beats a database, how partitions turn ordering into a tunable knob, and what exactly-once really costs. Includes an interactive delivery-semantics explorer — and the fourth quadrant nobody mentions, where you get neither guarantee.

item.title: Design Google Maps
item.author: abhaypratap3537@gmail.com (Abhay)
item.description: One billion daily users, 100 petabytes of map tiles, and a road graph too big to fit in memory. Routing tiles, the CDN economics of map rendering, adaptive rerouting — plus an interactive tile explorer, and why the real tile URL is not what the textbook says.
